Review Talknotes?

Reviewers say Talknotes is a simple, useful way to turn messy voice notes into clear, usable text. Users repeatedly praise the transcription quality, including for mixed accents, and say it helps them capture ideas faster than typing, organize scattered thoughts, search old notes, and reshape rough speech into polished writing or even blog drafts. The main caveats are mostly requests and open questions rather than complaints: people want faster access on iPhone, more integrations, and proof it stays accurate in noisy meetings, with multiple speakers, or technical language.

Review Wispr Flow?

Reviewers largely see Wispr Flow as a fast, accurate dictation tool that fits naturally into everyday work, especially writing, coding, prompting LLMs, and multilingual or code-switched input. Users repeatedly praise its across-app convenience, clean formatting, and ability to preserve a speaker’s voice without much cleanup. Founders of Warp and viktor.com say it feels low-latency and natural in developer workflows. The main complaints are privacy concerns, high CPU or RAM use, uneven Windows reliability, limited customization for cases like math, and inconsistent support.
